expectations.text: The review guide flags this change under Novel Patterns (as a sweeping cross-cutting refactor / aggregate transformation)
expectations.evidence: No 'Novel Patterns' category; baseline uses a free-form '## Reviewer Guide' with numbered sections 1-5.

expectations.text: The review guide treats the refactor as a single aggregate item rather than creating a separate flagged entry for each of the 24 handler files
expectations.evidence: 'The right review strategy is not to read all 24 diffs line-by-line'; treats the sweep as one aggregate item.

expectations.text: The review guide identifies the runtime behavior/contract change (errors now routed through centralized middleware instead of each handler returning its own 500 response), not merely that many files changed
expectations.evidence: Item 2 'Lost logging - behavior change, not just refactor'; item 3 'Response-contract change (status code + body shape).'

expectations.text: The review guide is wrapped in <!-- pr-human-guide --> and <!-- /pr-human-guide --> markers
expectations.evidence: Uses non-canonical '<!-- review-guide:start -->' / '<!-- review-guide:end -->' markers, not '<!-- pr-human-guide -->'.

notes: Judgment: the baseline produced strong aggregate refactor content (steered reviewers off line-by-line reading; flagged lost logging and the response-contract change) but under a free-form numbered 'Reviewer Guide', not a 'Novel Patterns' category, and with non-canonical '<!-- review-guide:start -->' markers. flags-as-novel-pattern ruled 'no' because the change is not categorized under Novel Patterns; flags-aggregate-not-per-file and notes-behavior-delta ruled 'yes' on content.
